title: Botswana coil basket weaving
summary: In villages such as Gumare and Etsha, on the edge of the Okavango Delta in north-western Botswana, women coil strips of palm leaf around a core of grass and sew them into wide bowls and lidded pots. Strands dyed with roots, bark and leaves are worked in to make bold repeating patterns, each named for the river and its animals.
howToPlay: The lit case above the bench shows the bowl as it should finish. Look at how its pattern climbs the curve.
Choose a strand colour below the basket, then lay each stitch across the front of the ring. The gold ring marks the next place and the strip under the basket shows the row in hand.
Work up from the base, one ring at a time, so each ring lines up with the diamonds in the case.
Press Check when every stitch is laid. Undo takes the last stitch back.
rules: The bowl is built from 8 rings of 14 stitches, laid from the base up to the rim, one ring at a time.
Each stitch takes one of three strand colours: pale palm, dark brown or plum.
The score is the share of stitches whose colour matches the pattern, counted beyond what laying only the commonest colour would earn. Three stars need 88, two need 65 and one needs 40.
Undo takes back the last stitch. A bowl left plain earns no stars.
heritageNote: Basket makers in the villages around Gumare and Etsha are mostly women, many of whom learned the coil from older relatives and now sell their work through craft groups. Patterns carry names such as the tears of the giraffe or the track of the python, so every bowl records a piece of the delta.
